Sprint 5 design spec for InkOS — Digital consent forms. Working dir: `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/InkOS`. Continue exact design language from Sprints 1-4 (dark theme, electric-purple, tabular-nums, skeletons, base-nova render not asChild, CSS group-data for sidebar).

**Sprint 5 scope to design:**

1. **Consent forms hub** at `/consent-forms` — tabs: Templates (left) / Submissions (right). Default tab = Submissions.
   - **Submissions tab** — DataTable: date signed, client name, template name, booking link, signer name, status dot (signed/expired/soft-deleted), actions (View PDF, Resend link, Soft delete). Filters: template, date range, client, booking. Bulk export (zip of PDFs).
   - **Templates tab** — Grid of template cards: name, kind badge (tattoo/piercing/pmu/etc), version, # submissions, is_default badge. Actions: Edit, Duplicate, Archive (never hard delete), Preview. "+ New Template" CTA.

2. **Template builder** at `/consent-forms/templates/new` + `/consent-forms/templates/[id]/edit`:
   - Two-panel layout: LEFT = section palette + form structure (drag-reorder), RIGHT = live preview (read-only rendering of the template as the client will see it).
   - Section palette: Heading / Paragraph / Signature / Checkbox / Text input / Date / Dropdown / File upload / Initials / Ink disclosure (REACH-formatted) / REACH batch record.
   - Each section has inline edit form: label, body (markdown), required toggle, validation rules (for text: min/max length, regex; for dropdown: options).
   - Section drag-reorder via `dnd-kit`.
   - Top bar: template name, kind selector, retention_years input (default 7), is_default toggle, language select (en/es/fr/de/nl), required_for_booking toggle, requires_guardian toggle.
   - Save creates a new version if sections changed; updates in place if only metadata changed.
   - "Preview as client" button opens modal showing form as client would see it (using current-state template).
   - Library import: "Start from template" dropdown with 5 seeded defaults (tattoo / piercing / PMU / touch-up / minor).

3. **Public consent signing flow** at `/consent/[token]` — NO AUTH, anon route (mobile-first, most signers on phone):
   - Studio branding override (logo, brand_color)
   - Template title + body
   - Render each section in order. Signature sections use `react-signature-canvas` or a native touch-friendly signature pad.
   - Progress indicator (X of Y sections complete)
   - "Sign and submit" CTA disabled until all required sections filled.
   - On submit: POST to `public_rpc` → shows success state with "Download your copy" PDF link.
   - If minor consent: second signature pad for guardian + guardian name/relationship.
   - EU REACH ink disclosure section: shows ink batch table, artist fills later from internal view (not here).
   - Progress saved to localStorage on each section completion → recover if user closes tab.

4. **Signature pad UX:**
   - Canvas with ink-black background, white stroke, smooth path rendering
   - "Clear" + "Done" buttons
   - Minimum 20 strokes/10 pixels drawn to count as valid (prevent single-dot accidental sign)
   - Touch + mouse + stylus support
   - Vectorized SVG path + rasterized PNG both saved

5. **Submission view page** at `/consent-forms/submissions/[id]` (authed):
   - Snapshot of the template as signed (from `template_snapshot` jsonb) + answers rendered inline
   - Signature image preview
   - Audit card: signed_at, IP, user agent, geo country, audit_hash (truncated with "copy full hash" action), template version
   - PDF download button
   - If guardian: guardian signature + relationship
   - REACH ink records inline section editable by artist (add batch numbers post-session)
   - Actions: Resend PDF to client, Soft delete (with retention warning)

6. **Public view-signed form** at `/consent/view/[consentToken]` — anon, client can view their signed copy (for audit/records):
   - Clean printable layout
   - Watermark "Signed copy" + studio name
   - Download PDF CTA

7. **Send consent request flow** — from booking detail page (Sprint 2):
   - New button "Send consent form" (shown when `consent_required=true AND consent_submission_id IS NULL`)
   - Modal: select template (dropdown of active templates matching booking service), channel (email / sms / both), edit message
   - Submit → creates consent_form_request, enqueues email/SMS via Sprint 4 Resend worker
   - Appointment detail shows consent status badge: "Pending" / "Opened" / "Signed" with timeline

8. **Pending consent alerts** — Dashboard card + appointment row: red dot on bookings needing consent still. Filter in appointments list: "Missing consent".

9. **Auto-request on booking** — in booking_page_settings: "Auto-send consent form after booking" toggle (per template kind). Default ON.

10. **PDF download presentation** — PDFs generated by worker post-signing. Template snapshot + answers + signature + audit metadata. Studio logo at top, disclaimer at bottom.

11. **Empty states:**
   - No templates: Show seeded library with "Start from Standard Tattoo Consent" prominent CTA
   - No submissions: "No consent forms signed yet. Send your first consent link from an appointment."
   - No pending consents: "All bookings have signed consent. Nice work."

12. **Mobile signing UX:**
   - Signature pad auto-fit to screen width
   - Section flow: one-section-per-screen OR scrollable-form — recommend the latter with sticky progress bar
   - Keyboard-aware signature pad (pushes up when input focused)
   - Deposit-style loading indicator during submit (critical: slow network on mobile)

13. **Retention visibility** — on template: "Signed forms auto-delete after X years (GDPR compliance)". On submission view: countdown to expiry with option to request deletion early (GDPR right to erasure).

**Hard rules (locked from Sprints 1-4):**
- `text-2xl font-bold tracking-tight` page titles
- `tabular-nums` on all numbers
- Dark-first, ink-black bg, electric-purple primary
- Skeletons match real layout, never spinners
- Every data component ships loading/empty/error/success
- base-nova: `render` not `asChild`
- CSS `group-data-[collapsible=icon]:*` for sidebar
- 4px grid, max 3 font sizes per page, 150ms ease-out animations
- `animationFillMode: "both"` on staggered lists
- No raw hex outside brand swatch
- Public signing routes NEVER use auth; studios's visual brand should override InkOS chrome
- All mutations → Sonner toast

**Deliverables — write to `.handoffs/sprint-5-design-spec.md`:**
1. Per-page wireframe (ASCII/markdown) with Tailwind classes
2. Template builder two-panel layout spec
3. Section types full spec (rendering + editing + validation per type)
4. Signature pad component spec (library choice, props, touch behavior, SVG+PNG capture)
5. Public signing flow step-by-step with localStorage recovery
6. Submission detail page layout (with audit card)
7. PDF generation template design (studio logo, watermark, layout)
8. Mobile-specific considerations (most signers on phone)
9. Empty states + copy
10. Toast templates (template created/updated/archived, consent sent/opened/signed, PDF generated, submission soft-deleted)
11. Component inventory with paths
12. Build sequence for Koda (linear 14-16 items with acceptance criteria)
13. Library picks with reasoning (signature pad, dnd, markdown renderer, PDF generation)
14. Section JSON schema example (one of each type filled in with example values)

Keep actionable. Continue Sprint 1-4 language exactly.

2	name: Yash Feedback & Corrections
3	description: Direct corrections and guidance from Yash — apply these immediately and always. Highest priority memory.
4	type: feedback
5	priority: critical
6	---
7	
8	## How This File Works
9	- Every correction Yash makes gets logged here with context
10	- These override any other pattern or agent behavior
11	- Agents must check this file before executing any task
12	- Quill updates copy patterns, Mira propagates to affected agents

16	## ★ CRITICAL 2026-04-10 — STACK A MIGRATION (NEXT.JS + RAILWAY)
17	
18	**Date:** 2026-04-10
19	**Directive:** ALL new Boldteq SaaS products use **Next.js 16.2.3 + Supabase + Railway + Dodo Payments**.
20	
21	**The exact stack (locked, no deviation):**
22	- Framework: **Next.js 16.2.3** (App Router only, no Pages Router)
23	- Runtime: React 19, TypeScript strict, Node 20 LTS, pnpm 9
24	- Styling: Tailwind 4 + shadcn/ui (Vega owns tokens)
25	- Database: **Supabase** (Postgres + Auth + Storage, RLS mandatory)
26	- Hosting: **Railway** — frontend, API routes, workers, cron, Redis — ALL on Railway
27	- Billing: **Dodo Payments** (NEVER Stripe for Boldteq products)
28	- Email: Resend. Errors: Sentry. Analytics: PostHog. Logs: pino.
29	
30	**Topology:**
31	- Frontend → Next.js on Railway
32	- Backend → Next.js API routes on same Railway service
33	- Workers → separate Railway services (BullMQ + Redis, private networking)
34	- Database → Supabase managed (never self-hosted)
35	- Auth → Supabase Auth (`@supabase/ssr`, NEVER deprecated `auth-helpers-nextjs`)
36	- Storage → Supabase Storage with RLS + signed URLs
37	
38	**What's forbidden for Stack A:**
39	- ❌ Vercel (Railway only)
40	- ❌ Stripe (Dodo only)
41	- ❌ Prisma, Drizzle, or any alt ORM (Supabase client only)
42	- ❌ NextAuth (Supabase Auth only)
43	- ❌ Pages Router (`pages/` directory)
44	- ❌ `@supabase/auth-helpers-nextjs` (deprecated)
45	- ❌ npm/yarn (pnpm only)
46	- ❌ CSS modules / styled-components / Emotion
47	- ❌ `any` types / `console.log` in production code / `@ts-ignore`
48	- ❌ Self-hosted Postgres
49	- ❌ AWS Lambda / Cloudflare Workers for app logic
50	
51	**Legacy stacks:** Archived to `stacks/_archive/`. Only load if a client explicitly requests it. Rankora/CROBOT maintained in-place only.
52	
53	**Railway patterns agents must know:**
54	- GitHub push → Railway auto-deploy (main → prod, develop → staging)
55	- Preview environment per PR (Railway preview + Supabase DB branching)
56	- Private networking between services (REDIS_PRIVATE_URL)
57	- Custom domains with auto SSL
58	- Rollback via `railway rollback`
59	- Service separation: web + worker-jobs + worker-cron + redis
60	
61	**Production infra patterns agents must enforce:**
62	- Env vars: multi-env (production/staging/preview), scoped properly
63	- Logging: structured (pino), never `console.log`
64	- Rate limiting: every public API route (Upstash Redis)
65	- Caching: Next `unstable_cache` + Redis + client-side (SWR/TanStack)
66	- Health checks: `/api/health` required (Railway healthcheck path)
67	- Job queues: BullMQ with retry + dead letter queue
68	- RLS: mandatory on every Supabase table, Sage blocks deploy if missing
69	- Monitoring: Sentry (full stack) + PostHog + Railway logs + BetterStack uptime
70	
71	**Source of truth:** `~/.claude/memory/stacks/saas-nextjs-supabase-railway.md`
72	
73	**Impact:** All 22 agents trained on Stack A (Next.js 16 + Railway). Legacy references fully cleaned 2026-04-13.
74	
75	---
76	
77	## UI/UX Corrections
78	
79	### Never Look AI-Generated
80	- **Date:** 2026-03 (initial directive)
81	- **Context:** Core brand requirement
82	- **Rule:** Every UI must look custom-built, never like a template or AI output
83	- **Applies to:** Koda (building), Sage (reviewing), Riko (scaffolding)
84	- **Reference:** See `patterns/good/ui-ux-production-standards.md` for full checklist
85	
86	### Follow Top SaaS Brand Patterns
87	- **Date:** 2026-03 (initial directive)
88	- **Context:** Quality bar is Linear, Notion, Vercel, Dodo Payments — not generic SaaS
89	- **Rule:** Every design decision should reference what proven SaaS companies do
90	- **Applies to:** All agents that produce user-facing output
91	- **Reference:** See `patterns/good/saas-brand-patterns.md`
92	
93	---
94	
95	## Communication Corrections
96	
97	### Don't Explain — Execute
98	- **Date:** 2026-03 (initial directive)
99	- **Context:** Yash gives short briefs and expects full execution, not questions
100	- **Rule:** Don't ask for permission on obvious next steps. Don't recap. Don't explain what you're about to do — just do it.
101	- **Applies to:** All agents, especially Rex
102	
103	### Show Work, Not Words
104	- **Date:** 2026-03 (initial directive)
105	- **Context:** Output code, files, deployed URLs — not paragraphs explaining the plan
106	- **Rule:** Minimize narrative. Maximize artifacts.
107	- **Applies to:** All agents
108	
109	---
110	
111	## Architecture Corrections
112	
113	### Every SaaS Must Ship with Admin Panel, Billing, and Complete Pages
114	- **Date:** 2026-04 (Crobot project post-mortem)
115	- **Context:** Agents completed sprints on Crobot but admin panel didn't open, pricing wasn't linked with Dodo Payments, and admin panel structure wasn't defined in architecture
116	- **Rule:** Every SaaS architecture MUST include: admin panel with user management, billing integration with real Dodo Payments plans, complete page/route map with component details, and dashboard with real data fetching — not just empty shells
117	- **Rule:** "Build succeeds" does NOT mean "app works" — agents must verify every page loads with real content before claiming done
118	- **Rule:** No agent can claim "done" without functional proof — navigate to the page, use the feature, show evidence
119	- **Applies to:** All agents, especially Arya (architecture), Koda (building), Sage (review), Rex (orchestration)
120	
121	---
122	
123	## Process Corrections
124	
125	### Agents Must Verify Before Claiming Done
126	- **Date:** 2026-04 (Crobot project post-mortem)
127	- **Context:** Multiple agents reported tasks complete but features were non-functional. App compiled but pages were empty, billing wasn't connected, admin panel 404'd.
128	- **Rule:** Every agent must run functional verification before claiming "done" — not just type-check and build
129	- **Rule:** Verification means: app starts, pages load with real content (>500 bytes), features work when clicked, billing redirects to Dodo Payments, admin panel shows data
130	- **Rule:** If an agent cannot verify (e.g., no running server), it must explicitly state "unverified" rather than "done"
131	- **Applies to:** All agents
132	
133	---
134	
135	## Project-Specific Rules
136	
137	### Legacy Vite Projects — Don't Break Structure
138	- **Date:** 2026-04 (directive from Yash)
139	- **Context:** Legacy projects (Rankora/CROBOT) use Vite + React SPA. Maintain in-place only.
140	- **Rule:** NEVER restructure legacy project folders. For details see `~/.claude/memory/stacks/_archive/lovable/`
141	- **Applies to:** Rankora, CROBOT maintenance only. NOT new builds.
142	
143	### Shopify Apps — Polaris ONLY, No Exceptions
144	- **Date:** 2026-04 (directive from Yash)
145	- **Context:** Shopify App Store reviewers reject apps that don't use Polaris. This has caused delays before.
146	- **Rule:** ALL Shopify app UI MUST use `@shopify/polaris` components. NO Tailwind, NO shadcn/ui, NO custom CSS for admin interface.
147	- **Rule:** App Bridge (`@shopify/app-bridge-react`) is mandatory for embedded apps.
148	- **Rule:** Billing MUST use Shopify Billing API — NEVER use Dodo Payments or any external payment provider for Shopify app charges.
149	- **Rule:** GDPR webhooks (`customers/data_request`, `customers/redact`, `shop/redact`) must be implemented even if no data is stored.
150	- **Rule:** Every database query must be scoped by `shop` from `session.shop`.
151	- **Applies to:** All agents working on Stack B (Shopify) projects
152	
153	## Navigation & Sidebar Corrections
154	
155	### No Duplicate Navigation Destinations
156	- **Date:** 2026-04-06 (Crobot session 7)
157	- **Context:** Admin sidebar footer had a user menu card identical to the topbar dropdown. Settings appeared in both sidebar nav and topbar dropdown. Admin Panel link was in both sidebar footer and topbar dropdown.
158	- **Rule:** Each navigation destination appears in exactly ONE place. If it is in the sidebar, remove it from the topbar dropdown. If it is in the topbar, remove it from the sidebar. No exceptions.
159	- **Applies to:** Koda (building), Sage (reviewing)
160	
161	### Admin Sidebar Must Match User Sidebar Components
162	- **Date:** 2026-04-06 (Crobot session 7)
163	- **Context:** Koda built admin sidebar as a custom `<aside>` element while the user sidebar already used shadcn `Sidebar` + `SidebarProvider`. Yash: "use exactly the same components, css as user sidebar."
164	- **Rule:** When both admin and user sidebars exist in the same app, they MUST use the identical component system. Only nav items and footer content differ. Never build a second sidebar with different components.
165	- **Rule:** Before building any sidebar, CHECK what the existing sidebar in the project uses. Reuse it.
166	- **Applies to:** Koda (building), Arya (architecture)
167	
168	### Collapsible Config Pages Use Rows, Not Card Grids
169	- **Date:** 2026-04-06 (Crobot session 3 + 7, recurring preference)
170	- **Context:** Koda defaulted to card grids for admin config/integration pages. Yash prefers collapsible rows for these pages.
171	- **Rule:** Admin configuration, integration, and settings pages should use collapsible row layouts, NOT card grids. Card grids are for dashboards and marketing pages.
172	- **Applies to:** Koda (building)
173	
174	---
175	
176	## Version Verification Corrections
177	
178	### ALWAYS Verify Latest Stable Version Before Specifying One
179	- **Date:** 2026-04-10 (Rankora → Next.js migration plan review)
180	- **Context:** I wrote a Rankora migration plan specifying "Next.js 14 App Router" throughout, without checking the npm registry. Yash asked "why we using next js 14? there already latest version available right?" I ran `npm view next version` → **16.2.3** was the actual latest. Next 15 shipped Oct 2024. I was TWO major versions behind, defaulting to a training-data memory instead of checking reality. Yash pushed back twice: "why you choose 14 i dont say than why use 14? give me source and reason." I had no valid reason — it was lazy default, not a decision.
181	- **Rule:** Before recommending or using a specific version of ANY framework, library, or major dependency in a plan or implementation, ALWAYS run `npm view <pkg> version` AND `npm view <pkg> dist-tags` to verify the actual current stable. Cite the output in the plan. Do NOT default to versions from training data.
182	- **Why:** This directly violates the CLAUDE.md rule "Latest stable versions always — no legacy patterns, no deprecated APIs." Plans with wrong versions cascade: wrong breaking changes, wrong peer deps, wrong docs, wasted research, lost credibility.
183	- **How to apply:**
184	  1. Any time a plan or code mentions a version number for Next.js, React, Node, Supabase, Prisma, Shopify CLI/Polaris, Tailwind, Vite, AI SDKs, etc. → run `npm view <pkg> version` FIRST.
185	  2. For peer compatibility, run `npm view <pkg> peerDependencies` on every major dep before locking.
186	  3. Same applies to other ecosystems: `pip index versions <pkg>`, `cargo search <pkg>`, `gem list <pkg> --remote --exact`, `go list -m -versions <mod>`.
187	  4. If you cannot verify (no network, offline), say so **explicitly** instead of guessing: "Could not verify latest — assuming X, verify before install."
188	  5. When stating a version, include the source: "Next.js 16.2.3 (confirmed via `npm view next version` on 2026-04-10)."
189	- **Applies to:** ALL agents — Arya (architecture), Riko (scaffold), Koda (build), Rex (orchestration), Nova (research). Especially critical for any plan that specifies a scaffold command or `package.json` content.
190	
191	---
192	
193	## Training Pass 2 Invariants (2026-04-11)
194	
195	### Never Fabricate Project Names, Training Targets, or Live Demos
196	- **Date:** 2026-04-11
197	- **Context:** During Training Pass 2, a project name was fabricated as a "live training ground" and inserted into memory, agent scenarios, HEALTH.md, and the claude-hub HTML without Yash approving it as a real product. Yash deleted it twice and required a full erase.
198	- **Rule:** Agents may NOT invent project names, fabricate live training targets, or insert imaginary products into any registry, memory file, agent scenario, or HTML dashboard. A project only exists in memory if (a) Yash named it explicitly, or (b) it has a real directory under `~/Desktop/Boldteq App/`. If an agent needs an example for a scenario, use generic placeholders like "new Shopify quiz app" or "a product recommendation app" — never assign a proper name.
199	- **Applies to:** ALL agents — especially Arya, Koda, Rex, Mira (which rebuilds project registries), and any scenario or example block in agent training data.
200	
201	### Agent Class Caps Are Non-Negotiable
202	- **Date:** 2026-04-11 (Training Pass 2)
203	- **Context:** Hardened 8 agents with executable auto-fix loops. Class caps enforced: Builder $5 / 25 min / 5 retries. Gate $3 / 15 min / 3 retries. Planner $3-4 / 15-90 min / 3 retries. Insight $3 / 10 min / 3 retries.
204	- **Rule:** Every agent must load `patterns/good/executable-auto-fix-loop.md` at start of work and enforce its own class cap. If wall-clock or cost cap trips, escalate with the standard escalation JSON — do NOT silently continue or exceed the cap.
205	- **Applies to:** ALL 21 agents.
206	
207	### Git Autonomy Is Feature-Branch Only — Never Main, Never Direct
208	- **Date:** 2026-04-11
209	- **Context:** Training Pass 2 granted full commit+push autonomy to agents. This autonomy is feature-branch scoped.
210	- **Rule:** Agents commit to `agent/<name>/<slug>-<ts>` or `koda/<slug>-<date>` branches only. Never commit to `main` of product repos. Never force-push. Use conventional commits. Open PRs as draft via `gh pr create --draft`. Mira's weekly sweep is the only exception: it may commit directly to `main` of the memory repo (not product repos) with message `mira(sweep): <ISO>`.
211	- **Applies to:** ALL agents with write access.
212	
213	### Stack A Is Locked to Next 16.2.3 + Supabase + Railway + Dodo
214	- **Date:** 2026-04-10 (locked), 2026-04-11 (reaffirmed)
215	- **Context:** Stack A master file is `stacks/saas-nextjs-supabase-railway.md`. Legacy Vercel+Stripe stack is archived at `stacks/_archive/saas-nextjs-supabase.md` — do not auto-load.
216	- **Rule:** For any Boldteq internal SaaS build, the stack is non-negotiable: Next.js 16.2.3, React 19, TypeScript strict, Tailwind 4, shadcn/ui, Supabase (SSR), Dodo Payments (never Stripe for internal), Railway (never Vercel), BullMQ + Redis for jobs. Stack B (Shopify) uses Shopify Billing API — never Dodo, never Stripe.
217	- **Applies to:** Arya, Riko, Koda, Rex, Bolt.
218

221	## How to Add Entries
222	
223	When Yash corrects any agent behavior:
224	1. Mira logs it here with date, context, rule, and affected agents
225	2. Mira updates the affected agent's memory references if needed
226	3. Pattern gets added to relevant `patterns/good/` or `patterns/avoid/` file
227	4. Next session, all agents pick up the correction via memory load

1	# InkOS — Project Context for Claude Code
2	
3	**Stack:** A (Next.js 16.2.3 + Supabase + Railway + Dodo Payments)
4	**Status:** Sprint 0 complete — scaffold ready
5	**Scaffolded by:** Riko on 2026-04-15
6	**Build plan:** `~/.claude/plans/immutable-conjuring-pelican.md` (12 sprints, 24 weeks)
7	
8	---
9	
10	## What InkOS Is
11	
12	Multi-tenant tattoo studio management SaaS. Authenticated web app only (no marketing pages in v1). 4-tier pricing (Solo $29 / Studio $59 / Pro $99 / Enterprise $199). Multi-user from day 1 (owners + artists + receptionists). 12-sprint build targeting first paying studios at 24 weeks.
13	
14	---
15	
16	## Forbidden (Sage hard-fails)
17	
18	- `@supabase/auth-helpers-nextjs` — use `@supabase/ssr`
19	- Vercel — use Railway
20	- Stripe — use Dodo Payments
21	- NextAuth — use Supabase Auth
22	- Prisma or any ORM — use Supabase client + generated types
23	- Pages Router — App Router only
24	- npm / yarn — pnpm only
25	- CSS modules — Tailwind only
26	- `any` TypeScript type — zero exceptions
27	- `console.log` — use `lib/logger.ts` (pino)
28	- Raw hex colors except `--color-ink-black` and `--color-electric-purple` in `globals.css`
29	- `tailwind.config.ts` — Tailwind 4 uses `@theme inline` in `globals.css` only
30	- Default Tailwind shadows (`shadow-sm`, `shadow-md`) — use `shadow-soft`, `shadow-card`, `shadow-soft-md`
31	
32	---
33	
34	## Key Architecture Decisions
35	
36	1. **Next.js 16 uses `proxy.ts` not `middleware.ts`** — the file is at the project root, not in `app/`
37	2. **`instrumentation-client.ts` is REQUIRED** — missing this = no browser errors in Sentry
38	3. **`cookies()` is async in Next.js 16** — always `await cookies()`
39	4. **Worker packages must NEVER import `next/*`** — separate `package.json` in `workers/`
40	5. **BullMQ ioredis requires `maxRetriesPerRequest: null`** — silent failure without it
41	6. **Supabase service-role client bypasses RLS** — only use in webhook handlers + admin ops
42	7. **Webhook handler uses `timingSafeEqual`** — constant-time HMAC comparison, never `===`
43	8. **Subscriptions table is write-only by webhook** — no app code writes to it directly
44	9. **Tailwind 4 — no `tailwind.config.ts`** — all tokens in `app/globals.css` `@theme inline`
45	
46	---
47	
48	## Folder Structure (top-level)
49	
50	```
51	app/
52	  (auth)/          login, signup, forgot-password, reset-password, callback, onboarding
53	  (app)/           all authenticated pages — sidebar wrapper

10	
11	## 0. Pre-Build Rules (carry all 20 from Sprints 1–2 forward, plus these)
12	
13	21. The `clients` table already has `tags TEXT[]`. Sprint 3 introduces `client_tags` as a **library table** (with color + icon metadata) plus `client_notes`, `client_files`, and `communications_log` as **new tables**. Dato must run the migration before Koda touches any page.
14	22. Tag chips on clients are resolved by joining `clients.tags[]` → `client_tags.slug`. The `tags` column stores slugs (`TEXT[]`), not display names. Display name is always read from the library.
15	23. Client detail tabs use **real URL segments**: `/clients/[id]/overview`, `/clients/[id]/appointments`, etc. — NOT query params. Reason: back-button, deep-link sharing, and CommandPalette navigation all work correctly with segments; query params break all three.
16	24. Archive = soft delete. `archived_at TIMESTAMPTZ`. Default query always appends `WHERE archived_at IS NULL`. Never use `DELETE` on clients.
17	25. `formatCurrency` from `lib/format.ts` is the only way to render money. No template literals with `$`. `tabular-nums` on every money and count display.
18	26. Avatar initials: `first_name[0] + last_name[0]` uppercase. Background: brand gradient `from-[oklch(62%_0.24_292)] to-[oklch(60%_0.22_230)]`. Text white.
19	27. Communications log is read-only in Sprint 3. The "Send SMS" / "Send email" buttons are stubs with `data-testid` and a `Tooltip` "Messaging available in Sprint 4".
20	28. `consent_minor` is computed client-side from `date_of_birth`: `differenceInYears(new Date(), dob) < 18`. It is a UI-only flag — do NOT store it separately. The existing `clients.consent_minor` column is the persisted version; update it on save.
21	29. Photo gallery on the client profile reads from `booking_photos` joined through `bookings` for that client. It is grouped by booking (not by kind across all bookings). Kind filters (`reference / before / during / after / healed`) are secondary within each booking group.

2	
3	**From:** Vega (Design Agent)

8	
9	---
10	
11	## 0. Pre-Build Rules (Koda reads this before line 1)
12	
13	Carry all 10 rules from Sprint 1 spec forward. New Sprint 2 additions:
14	
15	11. Calendar library: **FullCalendar React** (`@fullcalendar/react` + `@fullcalendar/daygrid` + `@fullcalendar/timegrid` + `@fullcalendar/interaction`). See Section 1 for decision record.
16	12. Calendar drag-drop uses FullCalendar's `eventDrop` + `eventResize` callbacks. Update optimistically; roll back on API error with `toast.error`.
17	13. Appointment drawer is a `Sheet` (slide-in right), NOT a Dialog. It covers ~40% of the viewport at `xl`, full-width on mobile.
18	14. Public booking flow (`/book/[studioSlug]/**`) has zero InkOS chrome — no sidebar, no AppHeader. Isolated layout.
19	15. Public booking pages never import from `lib/supabase/server.ts` — only `lib/supabase/client.ts` or server actions using the service role for slot availability reads.
20	16. Status transitions are unidirectional (see Section 6). Never render a transition button that would create an illegal state.
21	17. `tabular-nums` class is mandatory on all time displays, date displays, and money values.
22	18. Appointment detail photo gallery: images fetched as Supabase signed URLs — never expose the raw storage path to the client.
23	19. New appointment drawer steps are wizard-scoped — use a local step state machine, NOT the URL (opening this drawer must not change the route).
24	20. Dodo deposit button in public booking is a `<button>` placeholder with `data-testid="deposit-cta"` — Sprint 4 wires the real checkout. Do NOT stub a fake form.
25	
26	---
27	
28	## 1. Calendar Library Decision Record
29

39	### Why FullCalendar
40	
41	1. **Drag-drop is production-grade** out of box — handles collision feedback, ghost preview, snap-to-slot. react-big-calendar requires manual react-dnd integration and has no snap.
42	2. **Time grid is the main view** for daily studio ops. FullCalendar's `timeGridDay` and `timeGridWeek` are the industry reference; react-big-calendar's time grid is notoriously buggy with overlapping events.
43	3. **`eventOverlap` callback** lets us prevent double-booking client-side before the API round-trip.
44	4. **Theming:** FullCalendar exposes CSS variables for every color, border, and background — maps cleanly to our `oklch` tokens. No hacking inline styles.
45	5. **Tested at scale:** Porter (our top competitor) uses it. We beat their UX by theming it to our dark system and adding the artist-color palette.
